rounds.text: Helloji Holidays Ltd exhibits significant fundamental strengths supported by historical compounding, as evidenced by a 3-year compounded profit growth of 84% [E17] and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 46% [E16]. The balance sheet is exceptionally robust, featuring a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x alongside zero borrowings, confirming the company is almost debt free [E27, E28, E40]. Furthermore, the business boasts a stellar multi-year return on equity track record, highlighted by a 3-year median ROE of 30% [E19] and a 3-year average ROE of 29.6% [E41]. Institutional confidence remains firm, supported by domestic institutions increasing their stake to 8.82% and positive institutional money flow [E32, E33], all while operating within a supportive Consumer Services macro tailwind [E51, E52]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -2.19 Cr in March 2026 alongside a -60% drop in TTM compounded profit growth [E18, E25].

The financial reality of Helloji Holidays Ltd reveals severe fundamental deterioration despite its modest headline growth metrics. Compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has collapsed to -60% [E18], while operating margins have degraded from 10% to just 3% over a three-year span [E21], with a four-year yearly trend pointing squarely downward [E22]. This operational strain directly translates into alarming cash flow generation, highlighted by negative operating cash flow of Rs -2.19 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -2.23 Cr for March 2026, producing a distressed cash conversion ratio of -1.75x [E24, E25, E26]. Furthermore, working capital health is rapidly deteriorating as debtor days have stretched from 54.6 to 72.3 days and working capital days have nearly doubled from 31.8 to 61.6 days [E44, E45]. Institutional confidence has simultaneously evaporated at the margin, demonstrated by foreign institutional investors slashing their stake from 5.81% in December 2025 to a negligible 0.07% by September 2026 [E31]. Valuation provides virtually no margin of safety at a P/E of 39.7x and an EV/EBITDA of 16.2x that exceeds the sector benchmark of 11.7x [E1, E11, E35]. Conceded: the company carries zero debt and maintains a 3-year median ROE of 30% [E27, E41].

Conceded: [E18] trailing twelve-month profit growth sits at -60%. However, this short-term dip occurs against a backdrop of exceptional multi-year strength, including a 3-year compounded profit growth of 84% and a 5-year rate of 46% [E16, E17]. Conceded: [E21, E22] operating margins have experienced compression and a downward yearly trend, yet the company maintains a robust 3-year median return on equity of 30% alongside a solid current ROE of 10.8% [E13, E19]. Regarding the cash flow strain and working capital metrics [E24, E25, E26, E44, E45], the business operates with absolute financial safety holding zero debt at 0.00x debt-to-equity and flat borrowings of Rs 0.00 Cr, which has been explicitly flagged as a positive by filed statements [E27, E28, E39, E40]. Conceded: [E31] foreign institutional holdings dropped to 0.07%, but overall institutional money flow is logged as positive due to domestic institutions increasing their stake to 8.82% [E32, E33]. Finally, while the EV/EBITDA of 16.2x exceeds the sector median [E11], the company operates inside a buoyant Consumer Services sector enjoying a clear macro tailwind with a tailwind score of +0.65 [E52].

Conceded: [E16, E17] 3-year and 5-year compounded profit growths are high. However, relying on multi-year averages obfuscates a severe collapse in current earning power, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of -60% [E18]. Conceded: [E27, E28, E39, E40] the company is debt-free. Zero debt does not insulate shareholders from operational deterioration, as operating cash flow and free cash flow turned negative to Rs -2.19 Cr and Rs -2.23 Cr respectively in March 2026, driven by a disastrous cash conversion of -1.75x and a ballooning working capital cycle extending to 61.6 days [E24, E25, E26, E45]. Conceded: [E32, E33] domestic institutions increased stakes and overall institutional flow reads positive. This optimism completely ignores an exodus of foreign institutional investors, whose stake collapsed from 5.81% to 0.07% [E31]. Finally, pointing to sector tailwinds [E52] does not justify a rich EV/EBITDA of 16.2x—substantially above the 11.7x sector benchmark—especially when operating margins have eroded down to 3% with a four-year downward trend [E11, E21, E22].
